routes: /qualification/save (local fixture for existing alert scheduling and notification settings, not a new product route)
states: Production configuration surface, real policy/destination state, payload builders, API adapters and CSS against synthetic local endpoints. Playwright 1.56.1; Chromium 141.0.7390.37 and WebKit 26.0, light/dark desktop and 390px/320px.

A rejected saved-policy read renders an announced load error and Reload settings instead of editable defaults. No policy or destination PUT occurs. Keyboard reload announces pending saved settings without editable fields.
A successful reload restores the saved cooldown, overrides and SMTP destination before admitting an edited save. A failed replacement context withdraws editing again.

All twenty final captures inspected: unavailable, loading, recovered, replacement-unavailable and pending-save states across four variants. New load/error/reload content fits narrow widths; inherited panel description truncation remains.
This local browser proof does not establish type-check, unit/full-suite, lint, production-build, native notification, real tenant, physical-phone, installed or release acceptance.
interactions: 48 assertion groups across four variants: failed/pending policy reads, keyboard reload, correct saved-state write after recovery, replacement failure, normal Save/Discard, pending policy/Apprise replies, retained newer inputs, duplicate-save prevention, dirty tab re-entry, rejection and deliberate retry.

The changed-source control retains click-time wire fields and newer dirty inputs through older acknowledgements. Superseded destination reads cannot replace fresh context or leave the obsolete loading indicator.

No page errors, unexpected API requests or Test/retained-queue Retry/Dismiss/Relay/provider calls. Browsers and preview server closed. Earlier issued/acknowledged writes are not cancelled or rolled back.
